claims.text: A ductile Ni-based interlayer can be used between W and CuCrZr.
Introducing a ductile Ni-based interlayer reduces interfacial stresses caused by thermal-expansion mismatch between W and CuCrZr.
Reduced interfacial stress from the Ni-based interlayer improves the joint's thermal-fatigue lifetime under fusion-relevant conditions.
W and CuCrZr joined without an interlayer exhibit high interfacial stresses.
W and CuCrZr joined without an interlayer are susceptible to cracking.
A Ni-based interlayer accommodates differential thermal expansion between W and CuCrZr.
Accommodation of differential expansion by the interlayer reduces tensile-stress concentrations at the joint.
A Ni-based interlayer has thermal-expansion characteristics intermediate between those of W and CuCrZr.
The intermediate thermal expansion and ductility of the Ni-based interlayer mitigate stress concentrations arising from the CTE mismatch between W and CuCrZr.
The Ni-based interlayer lowers crack frequency at the bonded interface during repeated high-temperature cycling.
The Ni-based interlayer prolongs joint lifespan during repeated high-temperature cycling.
A W–CuCrZr joint without an interlayer experiences more frequent interfacial fracture under thermal loads than a joint with a Ni-based interlayer.
An extremely thin Ni-based interlayer may be insufficient to accommodate strain.
An excessively thick Ni-based interlayer may compromise thermal conductivity.
High neutron flux may alter the properties of the Ni-based interlayer over time.
The optimal Ni-based interlayer thickness is undetermined.
Long-term performance of the Ni-based interlayer under intense neutron irradiation is undetermined.
